questions.question_text:
The times (minutes) for $7$ runners in a fun run, listed in ascending order, are:
$133, 140, 147, 152, 159, 165, 172$
Find the five-number summary of this data.

options.why: Used the midrange $\frac{133+172}{2}=152.5$ as the median instead of the middle score.
Included the median score in both halves, giving $Q_1=\frac{140+147}{2}=143.5$ and $Q_3=\frac{159+165}{2}=162$.
Averaged the smallest and largest times for the median and also kept the median score inside both halves when finding the quartiles.

questions.question_text:
The times (minutes) for $9$ competitors in a half-marathon, listed in ascending order, are:
$150, 157, 163, 170, 176, 183, 190, 198, 205$
Find the five-number summary of this data.

options.why: Included the median in both halves before finding $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.
Sorted the data in descending order instead of ascending order, which swaps $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.
Took one of the two middle values of each half instead of averaging them.

questions.question_text:
The times (minutes) for $10$ runners in a cross-country race, listed in ascending order, are:
$110, 118, 125, 132, 139, 146, 153, 160, 167, 174$
Find the five-number summary of this data.

options.why: Used the midrange $\frac{110+174}{2}=142$ as the median instead of averaging the two middle scores.
Left the two middle scores out of both halves, giving $Q_1=\frac{118+125}{2}=121.5$ and $Q_3=\frac{160+167}{2}=163.5$.
Averaged the smallest and largest times for the median and also discarded the two middle scores before splitting the data into halves.

questions.question_text:
The times (minutes) for $12$ runners in a fun run, listed in ascending order, are:
$80, 86, 92, 97, 103, 108, 113, 118, 124, 129, 135, 140$
Find the five-number summary of this data.

options.why: Took the lower of the two middle values for the median and each quartile instead of averaging them.
Swapped the lower and upper quartile values.
Divided the range into four equal-width intervals instead of splitting the data into four equal-sized groups.

questions.question_text:
The times (minutes) for $9$ runners in a charity fun run are:
$165, 142, 178, 151, 187, 159, 171, 148, 193$
Find the five-number summary of this data.

options.why: Included the median in both halves before finding $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.
Sorted the data in descending order instead of ascending order, which swaps $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.
Took the lower of the two middle values in each half instead of averaging them.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Sort the data in ascending order**
$142, 148, 151, 159, 165, 171, 178, 187, 193$
2. **Find the median, $Q_2$**
$Q_2 = 165$
3. **Find $Q_1$, the median of the lower half**
$142, 148, 151, 159$
$Q_1 = \frac{148+151}{2}$
$= 149.5$
4. **Find $Q_3$, the median of the upper half**
$171, 178, 187, 193$
$Q_3 = \frac{178+187}{2}$
$= 182.5$
5. **State the minimum and maximum**
$\text{Min} = 142$
$\text{Max} = 193$

questions.question_text:
The times (minutes) for $7$ runners in a $10\text{ km}$ race, listed in ascending order, are:
$102.4, 105.9, 109.1, 112.6, 116.2, 119.8, 123.3$
Find the five-number summary of this data.

options.why: Included the median in both halves before finding $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.
Sorted the data in descending order instead of ascending order, which swaps $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.
Rounded each value to the nearest whole number before finding the quartiles.

questions.question_text:
The numbers of goals scored in $9$ games, listed in ascending order, are:
$3, 4, 4, 6, 7, 9, 12, 15, \ldots$
The last number has been omitted. The range is $16$.
What is the five-number summary of this data?

options.why: Used the range $16$ as the maximum instead of adding it to the minimum $3$.
Included the median $7$ in the upper half, making its middle value $12$ instead of averaging $12$ and $15$.
Averaged the fourth and fifth values, $6$ and $7$, instead of selecting the fifth value as the median of nine values.

questions.question_text:
The times (minutes) for $13$ runners in a trail race are:
$126.8, 112.4, 139.2, 119.6, 146.0, 123.2, 132.6, 115.8, 126.8, 142.4, 119.6, 135.4, 129.0$
Find the five-number summary of this data.

options.why: Included the median in both halves; the upper half then has seven values with middle value $135.4$.
Selected the higher middle value $139.2$ in the upper half instead of averaging $135.4$ and $139.2$.
Removed repeated values before finding the summary, leaving eleven distinct values with median $129.0$, lower quartile $119.6$ and upper quartile $139.2$.

questions.question_text:
The ordered data are $2,5,6,9,12,16,22,25,31,35,42,45$.
Calculate the upper quartile.

options.why: Selects the lower of the two central values in the upper half.
Selects the higher of the two central values in the upper half.
Added $31$ and $35$ as $65$ instead of $66$ before dividing by $2$.

questions.solution_text: The upper half is $22,25,31,35,42,45$. Its median is the mean of 31 and 35: $Q_3=(31+35)/2=33$.
